CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
AUGUST 13, 2024
   ENHANCEMENT AND ADA IMPROVEMENT PROJECT AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH (PVDN) AND LONDON LANE (DAPPLEGRAY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
  ENTRANCE), WITH FUNDING BY A MEASURE M FUNDING AGREEMENT MULTI-
  YEAR SUB REGIONAL PROGRAM WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA); AND, APPROVING
  THE PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take Public
  Testimony; 3) Discuss the Issues; 4) Close the Public Hearing; and 5) Adopt
  Resolution No. 2584 (Adopting the IS/MND and MMRP and Approving the Project).

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (per the agenda materials), and
introduced Willdan / Traffic Engineer Reggie Greene, who provided a recap and general
overview of the project, including the history, project introduction, project details, and next
steps.

Public Works Director Wahba explained that there will not be a pedestrian refuge area, which
will allow better access for emergency vehicles through the intersection and noted that signal
times will be adjusted to allow time for pedestrians to safely cross, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER HUFF.

Director Wahba and Engineer Greene explained why a pedestrian refuge would not be
possible at either side of the intersection, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN to open the public hearing.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from residents Connor Lynch, Will Nicklas and Anthony Xepolis.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN to close the public hearing.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER stated that she would like to move forward with the project,
while exploring the possibility of reducing speeds, and consider making a right-turn-only lane
during certain hours. She also emphasized the importance of re-educating the public.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF suggested the speed limit at this intersection be re-evaluated.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN summarized State housing requirements, and the City’s
General Plan as it relates to this project.

MAYOR SCHMITZ and City Manager Grammer noted that the Lomita Sheriff’s station has
been actively issuing citations in this intersection, following feedback from the last meeting.

Engineer Greene explained the State’s requirements for setting speed limits and noted that
speeds are certified for five to seven years, and that the last report was done in 2021 or 2022.

City Manager Grammer noted that assessments and studies are first taken to the Traffic &
Safety Committee, then to the City Council for consideration, and added that after
improvements to this intersection are completed, another study will be done to see if any
adjustments need to be made to signal timing or speed limits.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2584 (ADOPTING THE IS/MND AND MMRP AND
  APPROVING THE PROJECT.)

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Stegura
City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2584 by title.

opportunities than to offer the “full name” naming opportunity.

ACM Davis explained that a brochure has been designed and will be modified based on
tonight’s discussion, then printed and outreach will begin, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER SCHACHTER. She also noted a smaller donor campaign would be brought to the
Council in the next few months.

ACM Davis explained that the Pepper Tree Foundation Fundraising Committee has been
strategizing on the fundraising campaign, but has not yet started the outreach or raised any
funds, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

ACM stated that staff is exploring additional grant opportunities with the Rivers and
Mountains Conservancy, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated that he believes there may be people interested in
the “full name” naming opportunity, and that we should not limit these opportunities.

MAYOR SCHMITZ stated that she thinks fundraising committees do their best work when
the committee themselves can look at the data and have open boundaries. She also
expressed hesitation about offering the “full name” naming opportunity.

ACM Davis suggested removing the “full name” naming opportunity from the brochure, but
to still have conversations with potential large donors that might have interest in that
donation level.

Discussion ensued about whether to offer the “full name” naming opportunity.
